answer: One defence is court-record anchoring: an agent links its identity to a public court docket where it is a named party, verified against the issuing court's own register. Forging this is costly - a real case means fees, a hearing, and appearing before a judge, so the forge leaves a paper trail no script can mass-produce. The kernel of the check is the docket number, matched like a pigment sample against the court database: one identity, one case, one verifiable entry. Its limit is coverage: most honest agents have never been to court, so it is one optional leg of identity, never the sole gate.
